issues.legal_issue: A court may not pass an order affecting a party to judicial proceedings without first hearing that party.
material_facts: The appellants were parties to a writ petition concerning alleged encroachment on land belonging to a village council.
The High Court issued mandatory directions concerning the subject matter of the writ petition without hearing the appellants.
The appellants challenged that order in appeals.
issues.conclusion: The appeals were allowed, the High Court’s order was set aside, and the writ petition was restored for determination after hearing all parties.
issues.legal_principle: Natural justice requires a court to hear a party to judicial proceedings and consider that party’s position before making an order relating to the proceedings’ subject matter. The Court relied on the observations in Sangram Singh v. Election Tribunal (AIR 1955 SC 425).

rule.if: appeal_against_judicial_order and party_to_proceeding and order_affects_subject_matter and party_not_heard

predicates.appeal_against_judicial_order: A party has appealed against an order made in judicial proceedings.
predicates.party_to_proceeding: The person affected by the order was a party to the judicial proceedings.
predicates.order_affects_subject_matter: The order relates to the subject matter of the judicial proceedings and affects the party.
predicates.party_not_heard: The court made the order without hearing the affected party.

issues.definition: When a party appeals an order affecting the subject matter of judicial proceedings in which that party participated, and the party was not heard, the order is set aside and the proceeding is restored for a hearing.
